ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Researchers used instruments to detect the changes in CO2 absorption by Arabidopsis leaves under light-dark transition conditions, recording one experimental data point every 2s and presenting it as points in the figure. From the information in the figure, what can be inferred as the approximate total (true) photosynthetic rate of the leaves, in μmolCO2*m^-2*s^-1? (Keep the value to one decimal place)

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Researchers used instruments to detect the changes in CO2 absorption by Arabidopsis leaves under light-dark transition conditions, recording one experimental data point every 2s and presenting it as points in the figure. From the information in the figure, what can be inferred as the approximate total (true) photosynthetic rate of the leaves, in μmolCO2*m^-2*s^-1? (Keep the value to one decimal place)
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the horizontal axis is time (s), and the vertical axis is CO2 absorption amount (μmol·m^-2·s^-1). The label below shows that 0 to about 300 s is the light stage, and after about 300 s it changes to dark treatment. In the light stage, most scattered points are concentrated around +0.4 to +0.6, which can be read as a net CO2 absorption rate under light of about 0.5 μmol·m^-2·s^-1. After switching to darkness, the scattered points rapidly decrease to about -2.0 to -2.2, indicating the CO2 release rate in darkness, whose absolute value can approximately represent the respiratory consumption rate. Then reason: The question asks for total (true) photosynthetic rate, not net photosynthetic rate. True photosynthetic rate = net photosynthetic rate + respiration rate. Estimated from the figure, the net photosynthetic rate is about 0.5, and the respiration rate is about 2.0 to 2.2, so the total photosynthetic rate is about 0.5+2.1=2.6 μmol·m^-2·s^-1. Kept to one decimal place, it is about 2.6.
